React decides whether an element is the same one as last time by comparing the component function. A component that is created inside another component is a new function on every render. React then throws the old subtree away and mounts a new one, so its state is lost, its DOM nodes are rebuilt, and an input in it loses focus.

The rule reports a JSX tag that is a local variable holding a function written in the component, the result of a call, or the result of `new`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function Form({ label }) {
  const Field = () => <input placeholder={label} />;
  return <Field />;
}
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function Page({ theme }) {
  const Panel = createPanel(theme);
  return <Panel />;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Field({ label }) {
  return <input placeholder={label} />;
}

function Form({ label }) {
  return <Field label={label} />;
}
```

Choosing between components that exist already is fine:

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Heading({ large, children }) {
  const Tag = large ? BigTitle : SmallTitle;
  return <Tag>{children}</Tag>;
}
```
